subject: Velocis Labs — technical fit check & policy config proposal
messages:

Subject: Velocis Labs — technical fit check & policy config proposal

Hi Amelia / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps focused on the integration surface you asked about (SDK + auth), plus model routing and policy configuration for your high-throughput inference use case.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workload: conversational summarization + clinical triage suggestions (~50 req/s peak, avg 20 req/s).
- Latency target: 200–300ms p95 for single-turn responses.
- Data controls: logs retained for 30 days, PHI tokenization at client side.
- Preferred deployment: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) in us-west with failover to hosted in us-east.

Proposed technical approach
1) SDK & auth: Use our Node + Python SDK for client-side batching. Auth via short-lived API keys + optional mTLS for your on-prem gateway.
2) Routing policy: primary -> local dedicated cluster (us-west). Fallback chain: if latency/SLO breach -> cheaper quantized variant (v-q8) in same region, then hosted regional fallback (us-east) if capacity constrained.
3) Structured output/tool calling: recommend function-calling schema v2 for triage actions + schema validation on Redwood side to reject malformed outputs.
4) Embeddings/rerank: embeddings stored in your vector DB (we'll provide embedding endpoint and a lightweight reranker pipeline to run post-generation).

Attached: redwood-policy-draft-v1.pdf — rough policy doc outlining routing tiers and cost vs latency trade-offs.

Next steps
- Marissa to share a short integration checklist and sample SDK auth code (by EOD tomorrow).
- Amelia/Samir to confirm whether you want mTLS or KMS-only for key management.
- Karthik to propose an initial routing policy (baseline + two fallbacks) and cost estimate.

If that looks right I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up to confirm which model variants you want pinned and to walk the policy doc.

Thanks,
Soojin

Thanks Soojin — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few clarifications: 

- The 50 req/s is peak for the triage endpoint only; other endpoints are much lower.
- PHI flow: we need to ensure token-level redaction before logs leave our VPC; KMS is preferred but we may need mTLS as an interim.
- Latency: 250ms p95 is our internal target (diminishing returns above that).

Action items on our side:
- I'll confirm KMS vs mTLS by EOD Tuesday.
- Samir will provide a sample payload schema for the triage request.

Appreciate the policy doc — we'll review and flag any constraints. Can we also see a quick cost delta between using the quantized fallback vs always using the higher-accuracy model? Our CFO wants a ballpark before we commit.

Best,

Hi Amelia — looping in the SDK artifacts. See two snippets below and a link to the repo: https://drive.google.com/velocis-demo-notes

1) Quick Node batch example (pseudo)
```
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
const batch = client.batch({ maxSize: 8, maxDelayMs: 30 });
batch.queue('triage', payload).then(res => console.log(res));
```

2) Auth guidance
- Short-lived keys (recommended TTL = 15m) issued by your auth service via our token exchange endpoint.
- mTLS: our SDK supports client cert validation; we'll exchange cert fingerprints ahead of onboarding.

I've uploaded a minimal sample to the drive (node/python) and added a short checklist: 1) Add RW_KEY to your secrets manager; 2) Test prefix-caching by sending a few warm-up requests; 3) Validate structured outputs with the provided schema.

I'll follow up with the pricing delta Karthik prepares so you can share with finance.

Great thread — putting the proposed routing policy and the quick cost sketch inline so we have a single source of truth before we iterate the PDF.

Routing policy (baseline proposal) - Primary route: dedicated us-west (model: rwd-clinical-1, fp16)
- Fallback #1 (SLO breach: latency > 300ms p95): quantized variant in us-west (model: rwd-clinical-1-q8) — saves ~45% per-token CPU/GPU cost, quality delta ~1–2% on triage accuracy in our evals
- Fallback #2 (capacity constrained or regional outage): hosted us-east general-purpose (model: rwd-gpt-medium) — ensures continuity but expect ~2x cost per token vs dedicated baseline for same latency window
- Region routing: prefer us-west for residency; failover to us-east only for availability (not for cost).

Cost sketch (monthly, approximate for triage endpoint at 50 peak req/s)
- Baseline (dedicated, no fallbacks pinned): $18k/month (includes reserved capacity amortization)
- With quantized fallback enabled (auto-evict to q8 when p95 crosses 250ms): $11k–13k/month (depends on fallback frequency)
- Always run quantized variant: $9k/month — but accuracy drop might be unacceptable for clinical edge cases.

Questions for Velocis to confirm
1) Acceptable accuracy delta for fallback (we recommend a guardrail: run reranker on top of q8 when confidence < 0.7).
2) Confirm KMS vs mTLS for initial onboarding (we can support hybrid).
3) Confirm retention policy for request logs (default 30d, option to extend to 90d with additional cost).

I'll convert this into a short table and update redwood-policy-draft-v1.pdf; happy to join your CFO call to walk the cost numbers.

Thanks,
